description: A CLI that runs a queue container: a listener takes messages from a source (AWS SQS, a REPL, or a fixed array) and a dispatcher handles each one — echoing it, piping it into a program's stdin CGI-style, or feeding a long-lived child process. Components are configured with a name plus relaxed JSON options, and npm plugin modules can register more. The full agent reference is embedded in the package behind `cqi llm`.
rules: cqi is a foreground daemon: it runs until stopped. Never invoke it in an automated session expecting it to return — start it in the background or hand the command to the user, and say how to stop it.
Consuming a queue is destructive. A message handled by the sqs listener is removed from the queue. Never point cqi at a production queue to inspect its contents.

Components are configured as one string, `<name> <jsonic-options>`, where the options are jsonic (relaxed JSON, quotes and braces mostly optional). Quote the whole thing as a single shell argument: -d "exec programPath: /path/to/worker".

Built-in listeners are repl (default), sqs and array. Built-in dispatchers are echo (default), exec and stdio. Container and logger both have only `default`. Any other name must come from an npm module loaded with --plugins, and that module must already be installed where cqi runs.
The exec dispatcher runs a program once per message, so a container pointed at a busy queue is a process launcher. Confirm the programPath before starting one.
-c / --containers runs that many listener/dispatcher pairs in parallel and multiplies the load on whatever exec starts. The default of 1 is usually right.
The sqs listener passes its options straight to the AWS SDK and sqs-consumer, so queueUrl and region belong there; credentials come from the environment of the process running cqi.
--jsonic changes how incoming MESSAGES are parsed, not how component options are parsed — component options are always jsonic.
There is no JSON output mode; logs are prose and -v makes them verbose. Judge success from what the handler program did, not by parsing cqi's output.
The complete reference is embedded in the package: `cqi llm` (Markdown) or `cqi llm --format json`.
